repo_notes.content: Generate the wiki for Perseus MCP version 1.0.2. Treat pyproject.toml as the canonical version source and describe 1.0.2 as a patch release focused on bug fixes, reliability, test coverage, documentation, packaging, and release-process improvements—not as a major feature release. Use the current src-layout package: the implementation is in src/perseus_mcp/server.py, the package entry point is perseus_mcp.server:main, and there is no supported root-level server.py launcher. Derive tool names and counts from the registered FastMCP tools in the current source; the current documentation groups 23 tools into passage/navigation, discovery, search, Scaife retrieval, and cache management. Clearly distinguish local stdio clients (such as Claude Desktop and Cursor) from ChatGPT: the checked-in server runs over stdio, while ChatGPT requires a separately deployed HTTPS /mcp endpoint and cannot launch the local command directly. Treat OpenRouter as an optional notebook-based LLM integration that requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY; the MCP server and its Perseus/Scaife upstream calls do not require that key. Explain that Perseus CTS and Scaife are separate upstream services whose inventories and edition URNs can differ. Prefer current code, tests, workflows, README.md, tests/testing.md, and docs/ over stale generated wiki text. Avoid duplicating the same material across pages: overview pages should summarize and link to focused reference pages. Do not claim a feature, transport, retry policy, authentication mechanism, or deployment mode unless it exists in the repository. Use exact file paths and source-backed statements, and call out upstream-service limitations separately from project defects.
